title: Europe is at risk of creating a human rights black hole with its ‘return hubs’ for migrants - The Guardian
snippet: # Europe is at risk of creating a human rights black hole with its ‘return hubs’ for migrants. After a vote by the European parliament, the EU’s return regulation is nearing adoption – promising “more efficient” returns and “swifter” procedures to deport unwanted migrants. This will give countries the legal runway to set up return hubs – that is, offshore facilities to process people deemed to have no right to stay in the EU. In the pursuit of ever stricter migration policies, the human rights protections that Europe was founded to uphold are increasingly treated as disposable. The decision to pave the way for extraterritorial centres should alarm anyone familiar with the human cost of these schemes in the past. Longstanding violations of the rights of refugees and migrants in Libya and Tunisia demonstrate that migration cooperation aimed at preventing arrivals to the EU will probably result in serious and widespread human rights violations if adequate guarantees are not established from the outset.

title: Europe's early heat wave led to a spike in deaths, may have killed over 10,000 - Greenwich Time
snippet: # Europe's early heat wave led to a spike in deaths, may have killed over 10,000. Heat that hit Europe exceptionally early and hard this year appears to have led to a spike in deaths, with well over 10,000 more people dying at the height of the heat wave than would normally have been expected, according to figures that are still emerging across the continent. Measures of what researchers call “excess mortality” — the difference between the normally expected number of deaths and the actual number — spiked in late June, when parts of Europe experienced record temperatures. Experts caution that it takes a while for a full picture to emerge, and that many heat-related deaths will never formally be recorded as such. The EuroMOMO mortality monitoring hub, which receives data from two dozen countries, gave an estimate of 14,260 for excess mortality from all causes in the week ending June 28, more than 12,000 of those deaths being among people age 65 and older.

title: EC to extend ETS to some flights beyond Europe from 2029 - FlightGlobal
snippet: ***Commission proposes to include flights up to 5,000km from centre of EU in its emissions trading system.***. European Commission regulators have proposed extending the scope of its emissions trading system (ETS) to cover some flights beyond the European Economic Area from 2029. The proposals, which would apply on flights to third-countries located up to 5,000km from the geographic centre of the European Union, stop short of including transatlantic services. The Commission had more than a decade ago proposed including all flights within, to and from Europe in the ETS, before reducing the scope of the scheme to apply just to intra-European Economic Area (EEA] flights when agreement was reached for the global CORSIA programme at the 2013 ICAO General Assembly. “The scope will be extended to cover all flights departing from an airport situated in the European Economic Area (EEA) and landing in third countries no further than 5,000 kilometres from the largest aerodrome in the geographical centre of the Union.”.

title: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak - Houston Public Media
snippet: # At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak. Congo's health ministry said the deaths were recorded out of the 2,344 cases confirmed as of Saturday. Thirty-seven new deaths were recorded in the previous 24 hours in one of the highest totals. BUNIA, Congo — At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak, the country's Ministry of Health said Monday, with 37 new deaths recorded in a 24-hour span Friday into Saturday, one of the highest totals. The deaths were recorded out of the 2,344 cases confirmed as of Saturday, the health ministry said. The Ebola outbreak that was declared in eastern Congo on May 15 is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. Congo's Health Ministry said in its latest update that 724 patients are currently in isolation and in hospitals, and that it is intensifying response efforts in affected health zones.

title: Fisheries Remain at Heart of Iceland’s EU Membership Debate - Iceland Review
snippet: # Fisheries Remain at Heart of Iceland’s EU Membership Debate. Iceland’s fisheries policy remains one of the most contentious issues in debates over possible European Union membership, with disagreement persisting over whether Iceland could negotiate exemptions from the bloc’s Common Fisheries Policy. * Fisheries remain a central issue in Iceland’s debate over possible EU membership. * Supporters and opponents of accession continue to disagree over the scope for negotiated exemptions. The impact of EU membership on Iceland’s control of marine resources has long been a defining issue in discussions about joining the bloc. Opponents of membership argue that accession would require Iceland to adopt the EU’s Common Fisheries Policy in full, transferring authority over fisheries management to EU institutions and leaving no room for special arrangements. They argue Iceland’s unique dependence on fisheries could provide grounds for negotiating a tailored solution or permanent exemptions. title: Fraud prevention fail: DWP staff steal £600k - HR Magazine
snippet: To prevent fraud, “good policies must be backed by practical controls,” said employment law commentator Amanda Chadwick - *©William/Adobe Stock*. Employees and contract staff of the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) stole more than £600,000 meant for benefits claimants in 2025-26, The I Paper reported on Thursday (16 July). A spokesperson from the DWP told *The I Paper* that its robust controls had seen “the amount of taxpayer money stolen through internal benefit fraud in 2025-2026 stand at less than half of what it was in 2024-25”. But fraud prevention starts with culture, not controls, Sarah Hyland, director at consultancy Pace HR, told *HR* magazine. *Read more:* HR staffer jailed for £650k tax scam using TfL employee data. Amanda Chadwick, an employment law and employee wellbeing professional who supports the CIPD HR-inform information platform, told *HR* magazine that “good policies matter, but they must be backed by practical controls.”. A spokesperson for the DWP said that the department took allegations of fraud “extremely seriously” and had taken appropriate action.
